pages.title: IPC and Type Contracts
pages.purpose: The typed IPC/RPC layer: Api/Streams contracts, MessagePort RPC protocol and wire messages, the preload piBridge, desktop IPC channels, and the trust checks gating every bridge.
instructions: Document the renderer piBridge surface and how the Host port is transferred.
Explain lease semantics, subscribe/event matching, timeouts, and error shapes (RpcError, ToolchainError, BrowserError).
Explain the sender-trust gating used by desktop IPC handlers.

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: Three-process Electron architecture, process ownership boundaries, main/agent-host/renderer/browser responsibilities, and the primary data and control flows between them.
instructions: Describe how the Main process supervises the Agent Host utilityProcess (spawn, snapshots, ping/liveness, restart budget).
Describe the renderer-to-host MessagePort channel and the main-owned WebContentsView browser as separate surfaces.

pages.title: Build, Test, and Packaging
pages.purpose: The build pipeline (main/preload/renderer), bundling config, test runner and test conventions, contract/security/toolchain check scripts, the verify gate, and desktop packaging/release tooling including the Windows SBOM and helper.
instructions: Explain CI workflow stages if established by the workflow file.
Explain packaging targets and the Windows managed-helper/SBOM reproducibility checks.
Explain the test convention (.test.mjs, node:test, --test-timeout), the unit vs workflow vs smoke/electron tiers, and which checks run in the verify gate.

pages.title: Change Guides
pages.purpose: Focused, source-grounded guides for representative maintenance tasks: adding an RPC method, changing a toolchain capability, adjusting a browser permission rule, and validating a change end-to-end.
instructions: Each guide must be a step-by-step maintenance procedure grounded in concrete files, ending with the verification commands to run.
Prefer procedures that touch the fewest ownership boundaries.

pages.title: Desktop Lifecycle: Startup, Window, Recovery, Diagnostics
pages.purpose: Main process lifecycle: startup sequence, single-instance lock, window/menu/tray/badge, deep links, Host crash recovery, renderer crash recovery, shutdown/quit cleanup, and diagnostics export.
instructions: Explain crash report collection and redacted diagnostics export.
Explain packaged startup validation probes and packaged-cleanup-fault validation.
Explain quit cleanup with the 15s managed-process deadline and browser dispose.

pages.title: Software Updates
pages.purpose: The update subsystem: adapter (GitHub Releases via electron-updater), UpdateManager state machine, automatic checks, download/install flow, install-time cleanup, and error classification/redaction.
instructions: Explain error code classification and redaction of updater errors.
Explain that update URLs and release credentials are embedded in production builds and never accepted from the Renderer.
Explain the Windows helper replaceable check before install and managed-process cleanup on prepareToInstall.

pages.title: Security and Trust Model
pages.purpose: The defense-in-depth posture: Electron sandbox/CSP, preload trust, IPC sender validation, path allowlists, credential vaults and secret stores, redaction, managed-process and browser boundaries, and threat-relevant invariants.
instructions: Cover redaction points (diagnostics, channel errors, update errors, browser network body redaction).
Focus on invariants enforced in code and tests, and state uncertainty where the repo does not establish a guarantee.

pages.title: Agent Host: Runtime, Sessions, Models, Extensions
pages.purpose: How the Agent Host embeds the Pi Coding Agent runtime: session lifecycle (new/command/state), model catalog and credentials, auth/OAuth, skills and plugins, and event streaming to the renderer.
instructions: Describe auto-title generation (silent LLM request, never touches history).
Describe model catalog refresh coordination, credential synchronization, and models.json persistence invariants.
Describe session start/command/state flows and the event binding model (ensureSessionEvents).

pages.title: Built-in Browser and Agent Browsing
pages.purpose: The main-owned WebContentsView browser: profiles and partitions, tab manager and restoration, network policy and CDP interception, agent authorization grants, permissions, downloads, header rules, secrets, and Advanced Browser Mode.
instructions: Explain how remote pages never get Node.js, the app preload, or the main renderer bridge.
Explain profiles (temporary vs persistent), grants (temporary session vs persistent), and Advanced Browser Mode preconditions.
Explain the capability snapshot flow from BrowserService to the Host and how agent browser tools are granted/validated per target-tool side effect.

pages.title: Messaging Channels: WeChat, Telegram, Feishu/Lark
pages.purpose: The external IM channel system: adapter architecture, config and secret stores, login flows, pairing/allowlists, session binding and Pi-session bridge, inbound policy and media staging, and outbound rendering.
instructions: Explain binding semantics, default account tool grants, and per-session vs bound-session isolation.
Explain secret storage via the main-process CredentialVault and redaction of channel errors.
Explain transport characteristics: WeChat/Telegram outbound long-poll, Feishu WebSocket; no inbound listeners.

pages.title: Managed Background Processes
pages.purpose: The process_* tool system: backend selection (POSIX groups vs Windows Job Object Rust helper), ownership/authorization, readiness, log buffering, reaper and crash cleanup, and capability gating.
instructions: Explain reaper journaling and Host-restart/quit cleanup deadlines.
Explain the capability gate (platform, reaper, helper, owner identity) and fail-closed conditions.
State explicitly that this is lifecycle control, not a security sandbox.

pages.title: Projects, Files, Git, and Worktrees
pages.purpose: The project/file experience: allowed-root file access policy, file listing/reading/preview/download, file watching, suggestions/index, Git status, worktrees, and HTML previews.
instructions: Explain HTML preview lifecycle (app://preview tokens, TTL, CSP).
Explain file watch leases and the files.changed stream.
Explain the allowed-roots policy and the FORBIDDEN access control used by files.* handlers.

pages.title: Session Storage, History, and Indexing
pages.purpose: How session files under ~/.pi/agent are read, parsed, cached, indexed, and paged to the renderer, including the session index, path cache, content cache, history cursors, and compaction.
instructions: Explain paging/cursor semantics (context, contextPage, entryContent) and the STALE_CURSOR error.
Explain the session index fallback path when indexing fails.
Note that session files are on-disk formats owned by the Pi Coding Agent SDK.

pages.title: Developer Toolchains
pages.purpose: Toolchain discovery, verification, private install, and runtime resolution for Node, Python/uv, Git/Bash, Bun, jq, and bundled rg/fd: catalogs, probes, installer, shims, and the snapshot pipeline to the Host.
instructions: Explain private installs into userData and why they do not modify system PATH.
Explain resolution by intent (project-command vs install) and bundled vs system candidates.
Explain the snapshot revision pipeline (Main scan → toolchain:init/changed → Host ack).

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical entry point: what the app is, where data lives, how to run dev/build/test/verify, and a task-routing map to the rest of the wiki.
instructions: Do not duplicate the depth of other pages; keep it a practical summary.
Include the routing map of wiki pages to maintenance/operational tasks.
